title: Structured Identity Experiment v1 -- frozen specification, per Sol/Hamm's direction after accepting the Handout 2.5 runtime audit gate (SAFE_TO_RUN_STRUCTURED_DECODING = YES)
note: This node records a SPECIFICATION, not an implementation or a result. No training, fitting, or model code exists yet. Status is 'provisional' (not 'confirmed') because the spec requires explicit Sol/Hamm sign-off before implementation begins -- this node itself is not the sign-off.

claims.statement: Design is an explicit factorial: modality {SPK, LFP} x representation {X_flat, X_temporal, X_structured} x model_class {M0 chance, M1 linear, M2 MLP, M3 structured, M4 M3+regularized} x control {none, unit/channel-order permutation, time-bin permutation, within-trial scrambling, exchangeable label permutation}. No single cell authorizes a claim alone -- only the pattern across the full ladder plus ablations does (see docs spec Section 10 decision table).

SPK and LFP X_structured representations are NOT the same design. LFP channel x time uses real probe/depth topology (channels are physically adjacent). SPK has no default unit-adjacency topology -- starting point is either a permutation-equivariant treatment of the unit axis (temporal filter per unit + pooling across units) or a genuine-metadata-ordered axis (area/probe/depth), never raw row-index-as-pixel-adjacency without an explicit, separately-recorded justification.

The presented-identity positive control must NOT reuse jnwb.decoding.decode_stimulus_identity as-is (it uses ungrouped StratifiedKFold(shuffle=True), found in Handout 2.5). Implementation must build the positive control on the identical outer-fold (leave-one-cycle-out), inner-validation, and permutation-null machinery as the main omitted-identity decode -- same code path, different label column. This was an explicit qualification from Sol on accepting the Handout 2.5 gate.

Every eligible trial carries five targets from jnwb.trial_ontology: Y_expected (expected_identity, primary interest), Y_previous (preceding_identity), Y_position (omission_position), Y_family (sequence_family), Y_cycle (cycle, used as the fold-grouping variable, not decoded as a target of interest). Every reported Y_expected decode must be accompanied by the same decode against Y_previous/Y_position/Y_family on the identical pipeline -- an effect present on Y_expected but equally present on a confound target is confound-attributable, not identity coding.

The original invalid random-CV result (0.601, confounded) must never be resurrected as identity-decoding evidence. But the observation that motivated investigating it -- cycle/nuisance structure possibly differing systematically across cortical hierarchy -- is preserved as a SEPARATE, explicitly-labeled exploratory hypothesis (Section 11.3 of the spec), never merged into the main H_flat/H_structured claim, with its own falsifier and its own future labyrinth node.

A 7-row decision table (spec Section 10) fixes, in advance, how every possible pattern of ladder results maps to an interpretation and required action -- including the case where M1 (the simplest model) already succeeds, which requires re-running the exact confound checks that caught the original 0.601 confound before any claim, not proceeding straight to M3 to 'confirm' a result M1 already gives.

issues: This spec is frozen but UNSIGNED -- Sol and Hamm's explicit sign-off is required before any implementation work begins, per the spec's own Section 11.4. Do not begin implementation on the strength of this node alone.

None of the structural ablations (Section 9.2), the SPK permutation-equivariant/metadata-ordered representation, or the shared-fold-machinery positive control exist as code yet. Implementing them is explicitly part of what executing this spec requires.
falsifier: This node's status moves from 'provisional' to 'confirmed' only when Sol/Hamm explicitly sign off on the spec (recorded as a reply/decision, not inferred), OR is superseded by a v1.1/v2 revision if a deviation is discovered necessary before or during implementation.
